claim: The successful integration of engineered gene circuits into host cells remains a significant challenge in synthetic biology due to circuit–host interactions, such as growth feedback.
source: The successful integration of engineered gene circuits into host cells remains a significant challenge in synthetic biology due to circuit–host interactions, such as growth feedback, where the circuit influences cell growth and vice versa.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field, supported by the broader context of the manuscript and citations throughout the introduction.

claim: Growth feedback is a mechanism where the circuit affects cell growth and the growth in turn modifies the gene expressions in the circuit.
source: More specifically, a synthetic gene circuit embedded in a host cell possesses an intrinsic coupling mechanism: the circuit affects cell growth and the growth in turn modifies the gene expressions in the circuit (Klumpp et al., 2009; Klumpp and Hwa, 2014; Boo et al., 2019; Scott et al., 2010; Ray et al., 2016) – the so-called growth feedback.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Growth-mediated feedback can endow a synthetic gene circuit with various emergent properties, such as innate growth bistability.
source: Studies have shown that the growth-mediated feedback can endow a synthetic gene circuit with various emergent properties, such as innate growth bistability (Deris et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A non-cooperative positive autoregulation system, when coupled with growth feedback, gains increased effective cooperativity, thereby resulting in bistability.
source: For example, a non-cooperative positive autoregulation system, when coupled with growth feedback, gains increased effective cooperativity, thereby resulting in bistability (Tan et al., 2009; Nevozhay et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Toxin cooperativity can be induced in multiple toxin–antitoxin systems by growth-mediated feedback.
source: In another example, toxin cooperativity can be induced in multiple toxin–antitoxin systems by growth-mediated feedback (Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The number of steady states in one gene circuit depends on growth feedback and resource availability.
source: The number of steady states in one gene circuit also depends on growth feedback and resource availability (McBride and Del Vecchio, 2020; Melendez-Alvarez and Tian, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Growth feedback can have drastically different effects on congruent circuits with distinct topologies.
source: A recent study has revealed that growth feedback can have drastically different effects on congruent circuits with distinct topologies (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: For the toggle switch, memory can be retained and the circuit tends to be refractory toward growth feedback.
source: For the toggle switch, memory can be retained and the circuit tends to be refractory toward growth feedback.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a prior study (Zhang et al., 2020) mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: For the self-activation switch, growth feedback leads to memory loss.
source: However, for the self-activation switch, growth feedback leads to memory loss.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a prior study (Zhang et al., 2020) mentioned in the preceding sentences.

claim: Adaptation is defined as the ability of the system to respond to environmental changes and to return to the basal or near-basal state after some time.
source: Adaptation is an important and widely studied functionality of gene circuits, which is defined as the ability of the system to respond to environmental changes and to return to the basal or near-basal state after some time (Knox et al., 1986; Tyson et al., 2003; Friedlander and Brenner, 2009; Ferrell, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Certain circuits possess biochemical adaptation if they contain at least one of two architectural classes: an incoherent feed-forward loop (IFFL) with a proportion node and a negative feedback loop (NFBL) with a buffering node.
source: Previously, it was found that certain circuits possess biochemical adaptation (Ma et al., 2009) if they contain at least one of the two architectural classes: an incoherent feed-forward loop (IFFL) with a proportion node and a negative feedback loop (NFBL) with a buffering node.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A design principle for circuits with four genes was uncovered for simultaneously achieving noise attenuation and adaptation: the circuit must have a sequential assembly structure.
source: Quite recently, a design principle for circuits with four genes was uncovered for simultaneously achieving noise attenuation and adaptation: the circuit must have a sequential assembly structure (Qiao et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: There are 425 possible circuit structures capable of adaptation among three-node transcriptional regulation circuits with AND logic.
source: There are 425 possible circuit structures (identified by previous research; Shi et al., 2017), and we study all of them to simulate and test their response under different levels of growth feedback.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research that identified these structures.

claim: Type-I continuous failures are associated with the violation of the precision criterion.
source: Type-I continuous failures, as shown in Figure 2a, are associated with the violation of the precision criterion.
evidence: This is a classification based on the computational results and illustrated in Figure 2a.

claim: Type-I continuous failures constitute the largest failure category among all possible circuit topologies.
source: Type-I continuous failures constitute the largest failure category among all possible circuit topologies, suggesting that the exact cancellation is fragile and the loss of precision is the most common dynamical mechanism behind growth-feedback-induced failures.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as shown in the pie chart in Figure 2.

claim: Type-II failures are the second most common type of failure observed in the simulations.
source: Type-II failures are the second most common type of failure observed in our simulations.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as shown in the pie chart in Figure 2.

claim: A considerable portion (17%) of the circuit failures are caused by growth-feedback-induced oscillations.
source: As demonstrated by the light green and yellow slices of the pie chart in Figure 2, a considerable portion (17%) of the circuit failures are caused by growth-feedback-induced oscillations.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as shown in the pie chart in Figure 2.

claim: Type-III and type-IV failures arise due to growth-feedback-induced oscillations.
source: Type-III and type-IV failures arise due to growth-feedback-induced oscillations, while type-V and type-VI failures are caused by bistability or multistability.
evidence: This is a classification based on the computational results.

claim: Type-V and type-VI failures are caused by bistability or multistability.
source: Type-III and type-IV failures arise due to growth-feedback-induced oscillations, while type-V and type-VI failures are caused by bistability or multistability.
evidence: This is a classification based on the computational results.

claim: Most type-IV failure cases are caused by either a saddle-node bifurcation of cycles or an infinite-period bifurcation.
source: A random sampling of the type-IV failure cases reveals that most of them are caused by either a saddle-node bifurcation of cycles (Strogatz, 2018) or an infinite-period bifurcation (Strogatz, 2018).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of type-IV failures.

claim: The fractions of failures caused by growth-induced oscillations can vary dramatically among different network topologies, ranging from approximately zero to about 80%.
source: The fraction of failures caused by growth-induced oscillations can range from approximately zero to about 80%.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as illustrated in Figure 3a.

claim: Network topologies containing oscillation-supporting motifs have higher fractions of oscillation-related failures compared to those without such motifs.
source: Network topologies containing any oscillation-supporting motifs (discussed in the main text) are represented by red triangles, while the rest are shown as blue circles. The majority of red data points have higher fractions of oscillation-related failures compared to the blue ones, mainly due to the presence of oscillation-supporting motifs.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as illustrated in Figure 3a.

claim: Bistability is observed in most of the circuit topologies (377 out of 425 circuit topologies).
source: In our simulations, we observe bistability in most of the circuit topologies (377 out of 425 circuit topologies).
evidence: This is a result from the computational simulations performed in the study.

claim: Multistability has been observed but is relatively rare compared to bistability.
source: While multistability has also been observed, it is relatively rare.
evidence: This is a result from the computational simulations performed in the study.

claim: All eight optimal circuits share a common set of links (motif), as shown in Figure 5b.
source: In particular, all eight circuits in this family share a common set of links (motif), as shown in Figure 5b.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, as illustrated in Figure 5b.

claim: The combination of the common links in the optimal circuits is one of the minimal topologies with perfect adaptation in a three regulatory logic.
source: The combination of these common links is one of the minimal topologies with perfect adaptation in a three regulatory logic (Shi et al., 2017) and is critical for the circuit to be functionally adaptable.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The eight optimal circuit topologies do not contain any inhibition link from node C.
source: The eight optimal circuit topologies do not contain any such inhibition link from node C.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of the optimal circuits.

claim: The motif shown in Figure 6c is beneficial for robustness, while an inhibition link from the output node C is detrimental.
source: This result suggests that the motif shown in Figure 6c is beneficial for robustness, while an inhibition link from the output node C is detrimental.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the computational analysis.

claim: The shared motif for the green group is strikingly similar to the optimal minimal network in Figure 5b, with the sole distinction being the self-activation link of node B.
source: The shared motif for the green group is strikingly similar to the optimal minimal network in Figure 5b (the orange group). The sole distinction lies in the self-activation link of node B.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis comparing the motifs.

claim: Every network in the NFBL family depends on the self-activation link of node B to achieve adaptation.
source: Every network in the NFBL family depends on this link to achieve adaptation (Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: For circuits within the IFFL family, the self-activation link of node B is not a necessity for adaptivity.
source: However, for circuits within the IFFL family, this link is not a necessity for adaptivity.
evidence: This is based on knowledge from prior research on IFFL circuits.

claim: The average node concentrations at the equilibrium for the network topologies in the red group are consistently smaller than those in the blue group.
source: We find that the average node concentrations at the equilibrium for the network topologies in the red group are consistently smaller than those in the blue group.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: All circuits with oscillation type of failures taking up more than 20% of failures belong to the red group.
source: All circuits with oscillation type of failures taking up more than 20% of failures belong to the red group.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: Growth feedback can induce or strengthen oscillations in gene circuits designed for adaptation.
source: A unique finding is that growth feedback can induce or strengthen oscillations in gene circuits designed for adaptation.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: Growth-feedback-induced oscillation may be a general dynamical mechanism that can negatively affect the robustness of gene circuits.
source: These results suggest that growth-feedback-induced oscillation may be a general dynamical mechanism that can negatively affect the robustness of gene circuits.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the computational results and comparison with experimental studies.

claim: Growth feedback has a highly sensitive dependence on the circuit topology.
source: In addition, our study has shown that growth feedback has a highly sensitive dependence on the circuit topology: even a small structural differences between two circuits designed for the same function can result in drastically different outcomes under growth feedback.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: 2092 circuits across 306 different topologies exhibit loss-and-recovery behavior where adaptation, lost at an intermediate level of growth feedback, is restored at higher levels.
source: Specifically, we identified 2092 circuits across 306 different topologies where adaption, lost at an intermediate level of growth feedback, is restored at higher levels. This is 1.4% of all circuits tested.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The failure scenarios for four-gene circuits are the same as the categories for three-gene circuits.
source: A remarkable finding is that the failure scenarios for these four-gene circuits are the same as the categories for three-gene circuits (summarized in 1), indicating that the growth-feedback-induced failure mechanisms identified in our work are general.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis extended to four-gene circuits, as discussed in Appendix 1.

claim: There are 16,038 possible three-node topologies in total.
source: Altogether, there are 16,038 possible three-node topologies, with 425 topologies capable of adaptation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1a caption.

claim: There are 206 network topologies in the NFBL family.
source: More specifically, there are 206 network topologies in the NFBL family.
evidence: This is based on prior research that classified the topologies.

claim: There are 219 network topologies in the IFFL family.
source: There are 219 network topologies in the IFFL family.
evidence: This is based on prior research that classified the topologies.

claim: The ratio of adaptive circuits is somewhat lower in this study compared to Shi et al., 2017, due to stricter adaptation criteria.
source: To make our results more convincing, we have adopted a set of adaptation criteria that are stricter than those used in Shi et al., 2017. Consequently, the ratio of adaptive circuits is somewhat lower in our study, with 4 out of the 425 network topologies not demonstrating adaptation.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological differences between this study and prior work.

claim: 4 out of the 425 network topologies do not demonstrate adaptation in this study.
source: Consequently, the ratio of adaptive circuits is somewhat lower in our study, with 4 out of the 425 network topologies not demonstrating adaptation.
evidence: This is a result from the computational simulations.
